scope.definition: Culinary vegetables and distinct cultivar/edible-part entries: leaves, stems, shoots, roots, tubers, corms, flowers, buds, immature fruits, gourds, pods, sprouts and regional indigenous vegetables. Fungi and edible algae are included but explicitly labelled as culinary fungus or sea vegetable rather than botanically as vegetables.
scope.default_nutrition_basis: Per 100 g raw edible portion where quantitative values are supplied.
scope.botanical_note: Several foods conventionally treated as vegetables are botanically fruits (e.g., tomato, pepper, eggplant, cucumber, squash, okra). They are retained because the dataset follows culinary/nutrition usage.
scope.variation_warning: Nutrient composition varies by cultivar, maturity, geography, season, soil, storage, edible portion and analytical method.
scope.null_policy: For less-common or regional vegetables without a sufficiently standardized value in the compiled references, quantitative nutrient fields are null rather than estimated.

field_notes.energy_kcal: Approximate food energy per 100 g raw edible portion.
field_notes.carbohydrate_g: Carbohydrate per 100 g; source methods differ between databases.
field_notes.fiber_g: Dietary fibre per 100 g; analytical method can differ between databases.
field_notes.vitamin_c_mg: Vitamin C per 100 g. Highly affected by storage and cooking.
field_notes.culinary_status: Clarifies items that are botanical fruits, fungi, algae, herbs, condiment vegetables or other non-standard botanical categories.
field_notes.data_confidence: High means core values are matched to standard reference composition; identity-only entries intentionally leave quantitative fields null.

primary_sources.name: USDA FoodData Central
primary_sources.note: Principal source framework for internationally common raw vegetables. Foundation Foods provides current analytical food data; SR Legacy provides historical reference composition.

primary_sources.name: USDA FoodData Central Downloadable Data
primary_sources.note: Foundation Foods April 2026 and SR Legacy April 2018 are available in CSV and JSON formats.

primary_sources.name: ICMR-NIN Indian Food Composition Tables 2017
primary_sources.note: India-specific analytical reference for commonly consumed Indian foods, including vegetables and leafy vegetables.

primary_sources.name: FAO/INFOODS
primary_sources.note: International food-composition standards, database directory, analytical datasets and biodiversity food-composition framework used for regional and underutilized vegetables.

primary_sources.name: FAO Food Biodiversity resources
primary_sources.note: Used as the framework for including indigenous, wild and underutilized edible vegetables without inventing missing nutrient values.

quality_policy: Do not infer quantitative nutrient values for a regional vegetable merely from a related species.
Keep synonyms/market names labelled when retained for searchability.
Do not treat raw, cooked, dried, canned and pickled forms as nutritionally interchangeable.
For clinical use, verify values against the relevant national food-composition database and the exact preparation/cultivar.
